summary.headline: KMEW Q1 FY27 revenue rose 138% YoY to INR115.41 crore and PAT to INR62.75 crore, driven by one-off-heavy dredging execution.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR115.41 crore (+138% YoY), EBITDA INR73.41 crore (+258% YoY, ~64% margin) and PAT INR62.75 crore (+466% YoY, ~54% margin). Management attributed the quarter to dredging execution at JNPA (capital rock dredging, completed) and Pondicherry Port (maintenance dredging). Management said revenue and profitability are project-driven and vary by quarter. FY27 growth guidance was raised to "northwards of 60%" from an earlier 30-40%. The company also secured a INR62.40 crore IWAI hybrid ferry contract and raised INR150 crore via preferential issue plus a INR100 crore block deal.

financial_highlights.value: More than INR1,300 crore: dredging ~INR240 crore, charter & hire ~INR850 crore, shipbuilding ~INR240 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Intercompany order book placed with Knowledge Shipyard

segments.name: Dredging
segments.commentary: Core segment and main revenue driver this quarter from JNPA capital rock dredging (River Pearl 47, completed) and Pondicherry maintenance dredging (River Pearl 18). Dredging order book ~INR240 crore; management expects ~INR200 crore to execute in FY27.

segments.name: Charter & hire
segments.commentary: Recurring revenue from tugs, mooring, pilot, patrol, survey vessels under multiyear port contracts; order book ~INR850 crore across 15 contracts. Management says it is 3-5% of revenue currently.

segments.name: Shipbuilding
segments.commentary: Order book ~INR240 crore across 4 contracts, including IWAI contract for 10 hybrid electric 20-seat ferries (INR62.40 crore, ~10 months, built at Saphale yard). Currently ~9% of revenue; 42 third-party vessels and 5 captive vessels under construction.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth now guided to northwards of 60% YoY, up from earlier 30-40%.
Dredging revenue for FY27 expected to exceed FY26 levels; management expects INR200 crore of the INR240 crore dredging order book to execute this year.
Target revenue of INR1,000 crore in FY29; management described it as the next milestone.
Shipbuilding expected to scale significantly from Q4 FY27 after Phase 1 of Saphale yard (14 vessels per year at Phase 1, 18 at full build-out); Phase 1 operational by end of FY27.
Operating (EBITDA) margins guided at 35-40% across segments; management said dredging margins will expand with volumes and it does not expect ~48-63% margins to persist.
FY29 revenue mix target: dredging 45-50%, shipbuilding 40-45%, charter ~5%.
capex_capacity: Capex of close to INR1,000 crore over roughly the next 1.5 years: ~INR250 crore for Green Tugs and green vessels, ~INR450 crore for dredging, balance for shipyard and shipbuilding.
Adding larger TSHDs, CSDs, backhoe dredgers and water injection dredgers; new dredgers of 5,000-7,000 cubic metre capacity cited for deep-sea (Samudra Manthan) work.
Saphale shipyard: Phase 1 to Phase 3 build-out to ~18 vessels per annum; Phase 1 alone 14 vessels.
Portfolio under construction: 10 accommodation boats, 10 work boats, 4 CSD vessels, 2 60-ton bollard pull Green Tugs, 10 hybrid electric passenger ferries.
demand_pricing: Management said dredging faces very little to no competition; it is selective, requiring entry barriers to be met, and targets EBITDA margins of 35-40%.

Bid pipeline results expected in 30-45 days; dredging bids to be executed over 3 years. Maintenance dredging additions of INR100-120 crore in FY27, rising to more than INR250 crore from next year; capital dredging additions ~INR70 crore in FY27 and ~INR150 crore next year.
Historical bid hit rate above 50% over the last 11 years; management said it cannot assume this will continue.
Management attributed peer DCI's margin trend to older equipment needing refurbishment, while KMEW's fleet is more efficiently utilised.
Green Tug contracts are with Visakhapatnam and V.O. Chidambaranar ports, 15-year fixed charter regardless of utilisation; EBITDA margin cited at 75% for Green Tug.
Export shipbuilding inquiries from Europe for ~3,000 DWT vessels under evaluation; payment terms still being negotiated.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 growth guidance including the INR60 crore revenue shift from last quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Earlier guidance was 30-40% YoY; management now sees potential northwards of 60% for FY27 on order book momentum.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the ~INR1,300 crore order book executes in FY27 and what is the margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: INR200 crore of the INR240 crore dredging book is expected in FY27. Management said margins will expand, not contract, though not at the 63% operating margin seen in Q1, which it described as not guidance (35-40% stays the guide).

qa_highlights.question: Why are KMEW's dredging margins rising while DCI's are falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DCI has older equipment needing refurbishment, while KMEW is better sweating its assets for efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: Subcontracting expense trend?
qa_highlights.answer: FY23-24 subcontracting was high because of a JV structure where KMEW was lead partner. Now projects are executed individually; FY26 subcontracting expected at 5-6% of turnover, mainly shipbuilding and ancillary boats.

qa_highlights.question: Dredging vs shipbuilding mix in 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Dredging 45-50%, shipbuilding 40-45%, chartering ~5%. Shipbuilding pre-subsidy margins 15-20%, post-subsidy expected to go beyond 35%.

qa_highlights.question: Is shipbuilding captive or third party, and how is working capital funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently 5 captive vessels (3 tugs, 2 boats) and ~42 third-party vessels. Working capital funded from stage payments (every 10-50% milestone), with no further loans needed; shipbuilding subsidy of 15-20% comes on delivery.

qa_highlights.question: Is dredging a moat given privatisation of ports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disagreed, citing perpetual government demand, DCI's 50-year role and tender structure (domestic below INR250 crore, international above).

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 margins (~64% EBITDA, ~54% PAT) are driven by one-off-heavy JNPA capital rock dredging and Pondicherry maintenance dredging; management says results are project-driven and vary by quarter, so track whether Q2 FY27 margins normalise toward the 35-40% EBITDA guide.

FY27 growth guidance raised to northwards of 60% depends on ~INR200 crore of the INR240 crore dredging order book executing this year and on bid pipeline conversion; bid results were said to arrive in 30-45 days, and management said it cannot assume the historical >50% hit rate continues.

Shipbuilding ramp depends on Saphale yard Phase 1 (14 vessels per year) being operational by end FY27 and on shipbuilding scaling from Q4 FY27; the INR62.40 crore IWAI ferry contract runs about 10 months.

Capex of close to INR1,000 crore over about 1.5 years, funded after the INR150 crore preferential issue and INR100 crore block deal; monitor capex pace and cash generation against the INR1,000 crore FY29 revenue target.

Competitive moat questioned: management says dredging faces little to no competition, but a shareholder argued privatisation of ports could allow private dredging; also export shipbuilding inquiries from Europe (~3,000 DWT) have payment terms still under negotiation.
key_quotes: So, our EBITDA margins, we have been guiding at 35% to 40%.
It will not be the same as 63% operating margin. It is not the guidance, we've always guided between 35% to 40%.
We believe the order book is streaming up well, and there is a potential in northwards of 60% for the current year now.
Dredging business is a perpetual business.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on growth and order visibility, giving a firm FY27 upside view (northwards of 60%) and reaffirming the 35-40% margin guide. It was noticeably cautious on the Q1 margin level, calling it project-driven and not guidance, and it was evasive on specifics such as the Green Tug IRR (referred to the IR team) and the timing of export orders.
